items.text: When a spirit tablet passes four generations, bury it, shift the remaining tablets westward, and place the new tablet in the eastern niche.
items.citation: Encyclopedia of Korean Folk Culture, 사당 祠堂 · 사당 · 내용
items.quote: 4대를 넘기면 사당을 벗어나 조매祧埋를 한다 — When it passes four generations, it is removed from the shrine and buried.
items.conflict: Exodus 20:3-5; worship belongs to God alone; no veneration of the dead.

items.text: Because the spirit tablets of the ancestors are kept in the shrine, conduct yourself with constant propriety and reverence.
items.citation: Encyclopedia of Korean Folk Culture, 사당 祠堂 · 사당 · 내용
items.quote: 자손들은 평소와 다름없이 예를 차리는 생활을 지속해야 한다 — Descendants must continue to live with proper decorum as usual.
items.conflict: Exodus 20:3-5; worship belongs to God alone; no veneration of the dead.

items.text: At dawn, visit the shrine to pay respects before the ancestors' tablets.
items.citation: Encyclopedia of Korean Folk Culture, 사당 祠堂 · 사당 · 내용
items.quote: 신알례는 주인이 새벽에 일어나 사당을 참배하는 것을 말한다 — The morning visit is when the master rises at dawn and bows at the shrine.
items.conflict: Exodus 20:3-5; worship belongs to God alone; no veneration of the dead.

items.text: When leaving or returning home, report to the shrine according to the length of absence.
items.citation: Encyclopedia of Korean Folk Culture, 사당 祠堂 · 사당 · 내용
items.quote: 출입례는 바깥출입할 때 사당에 아뢰는 의례이다 — The going-out rite is the ceremony of informing the shrine when going outside.
items.conflict: Exodus 20:3-5; worship belongs to God alone; no veneration of the dead.

items.text: Offer sacrifices at the shrine on New Year's Day, the winter solstice, and the first and fifteenth of each month.
items.citation: Encyclopedia of Korean Folk Culture, 사당 祠堂 · 사당 · 내용
items.quote: 참례는 정조正朝・동지・초하루・보름에 각각 지내는 제사이며 — The regular sacrifices are offered on New Year's Day, the winter solstice, the first and fifteenth.
items.conflict: Exodus 20:3-5; worship belongs to God alone; no veneration of the dead.

items.text: Offer seasonal foods to the ancestors on Qingming, Hansik, and Jungyang.
items.citation: Encyclopedia of Korean Folk Culture, 사당 祠堂 · 사당 · 내용
items.quote: 천신례는 청명・한식・중양 등에 절식節食을 올리는 제사이다 — The offering of new foods is a sacrifice presented with seasonal foods on Qingming, Hansik, and Jungyang.
items.conflict: Exodus 20:3-5; worship belongs to God alone; no veneration of the dead.

items.text: Report all significant family events, great or small, to the shrine.
items.citation: Encyclopedia of Korean Folk Culture, 사당 祠堂 · 사당 · 내용
items.quote: 고유례는 집안에 크고 작은 일이 일어났을 때 사당에 고하는 것을 일컫는다 — The announcement rite refers to informing the shrine when any matter, great or small, occurs in the family.
items.conflict: Exodus 20:3-5; worship belongs to God alone; no veneration of the dead.

items.text: In flood, fire, or theft, rescue the shrine first; move the spirit tablets, documents, and ritual vessels before any household goods.
items.citation: Encyclopedia of Korean Folk Culture, 사당 祠堂 · 사당 · 내용
items.quote: 홍수나 화재가 발생했을 때나 도둑이 들었을 때는 가장 먼저 사당을 구한다 — In flood, fire, or theft, first rescue the shrine.
items.conflict: Exodus 20:3-5; worship belongs to God alone; no veneration of the dead.

work: Encyclopedia of Korean Folk Culture: articles on lineage, succession, adoption,
heading: 외손봉사 外孫奉祀 … 참고문헌

items.text: Support and care for your aged parents-in-law, especially if they have no son.
items.citation: Encyclopedia of Korean Folk Culture, 외손봉사 外孫奉祀
items.quote: 김성일은 처부모를 모시고 살았으며, 장인인 권덕황이 세상을 떠나자 홀로 된 장모를 모셨다. — Kim Seong-il lived with his wife's parents, and when his father-in-law died, he served his widowed mother-in-law.

items.text: Perform the ancestral rites for your parents-in-law when there is no son, especially if you have inherited their property.
items.citation: Encyclopedia of Korean Folk Culture, 외손봉사 外孫奉祀
items.quote: 사위인 류소가 재산을 물려받아 권옹뿐만 아니라 흥해배씨의 제사까지 지내게 되었다. — Son-in-law Ryu So inherited the property and performed ancestral rites for Gwon Ong and the Heunghae Bae clan.
items.conflict: Ancestor veneration conflicts with worship of God alone (Exod 20:3-5).

items.text: As the daughter's son, perform the ancestral rites for your maternal grandparents.
items.citation: Encyclopedia of Korean Folk Culture, 외손봉사 外孫奉祀
items.quote: 대를 이을 아들이 없어 외손이 대신 제사를 지내는 것. — When there is no son to continue the line, the daughter's son performs the rites in his place.
items.conflict: Ancestor veneration conflicts with worship of God alone (Exod 20:3-5).

work: Encyclopedia of Korean Folk Culture: articles on lineage, succession, adoption,
heading: 기제사 忌祭祀 · 기제사 · 내용

items.text: Hold the ancestor's death-day rite at the first hour of the death date, giving it priority over all other affairs.
items.citation: Encyclopedia of Korean Folk Culture, 기제사 · 기제사 · 내용
items.quote: 파제일의 가장 이른 시각인 자시... 다른 모든 일보다 더 우선해서 조상을 받들어 모신다는 것이다. — At the first hour of the death day... to serve the ancestors before all other matters.
items.conflict: Ancestor veneration conflicts with the first and second commandments and the biblical prohibition on necromancy.

items.text: Prepare the offerings and write the memorial before the rite begins.
items.citation: Encyclopedia of Korean Folk Culture, 기제사 · 기제사 · 내용
items.quote: 제물을 진설할 준비를 하고 축문을 미리 써두는데 — Prepare the offerings and write the prayer in advance.
items.conflict: Ancestor veneration conflicts with the first and second commandments and the biblical prohibition on necromancy.

items.text: All present bow twice at the opening and closing of the rite.
items.citation: Encyclopedia of Korean Folk Culture, 기제사 · 기제사 · 내용
items.quote: 참사자 전원이 신위에 재배한다... 참사자 전원이 재배하는 것으로, 신을 돌려 보내드린다. — All participants bow twice before the spirit seat... bow twice to send off the spirit.
items.conflict: Ancestor veneration conflicts with the first and second commandments and the biblical prohibition on necromancy.

items.text: Burn incense, pour the wine, and offer the first cup, then bow.
items.citation: Encyclopedia of Korean Folk Culture, 기제사 · 기제사 · 내용
items.quote: 주인이 분향하고 술을 모사기에 세 번 따른 다음... 초헌: 주인이 신위에 첫 번째 잔을 올린다. — The host burns incense and pours wine three times... offers the first cup.
items.conflict: Ancestor veneration conflicts with the first and second commandments and the biblical prohibition on necromancy.

items.text: Offer the second cup; according to Zhu Xi, the host's wife does this, though an elder or the host's brother may do it.
items.citation: Encyclopedia of Korean Folk Culture, 기제사 · 기제사 · 내용
items.quote: 아헌: 『주자가례』에는 주부가 아헌을 하도록 되어 있으나, 집안의 연장자나 주인의 동생이 하기도 한다. — For the second offering, Zhu Xi's rites say the hostess does it, but an elder or the host's younger brother may do it.
items.conflict: Ancestor veneration conflicts with the first and second commandments and the biblical prohibition on necromancy.

items.text: Offer the third cup, as the honored guest, son-in-law, or elder does.
items.citation: Encyclopedia of Korean Folk Culture, 기제사 · 기제사 · 내용
items.quote: 종헌: 보통 귀한 손님이나 사위, 연장자 등이 한다. — The third offering is usually made by an honored guest, son-in-law, or elder.
items.conflict: Ancestor veneration conflicts with the first and second commandments and the biblical prohibition on necromancy.

items.text: Return the spirit tablet to the shrine or burn the paper, and burn the written prayer.
items.citation: Encyclopedia of Korean Folk Culture, 기제사 · 기제사 · 내용
items.quote: 납주: 신위를 사당으로 다시 모셔드린다... 분축: 축문을 태운다. — Return the spirit seat to the shrine... burn the prayer.
items.conflict: Ancestor veneration conflicts with the first and second commandments and the biblical prohibition on necromancy.

items.text: Wait in silence behind the screen while the spirit is thought to eat.
items.citation: Encyclopedia of Korean Folk Culture, 기제사 · 기제사 · 내용
items.quote: 합문: 조상이 음식을 드시도록 기다리는 절차... 참사자들은 부복하여 — Closing the door: wait for the ancestor to eat... participants prostrate themselves.
items.conflict: Ancestor veneration conflicts with the first and second commandments and the biblical prohibition on necromancy.

work: Encyclopedia of Korean Folk Culture: articles on lineage, succession, adoption,
heading: 시제 時祭 · 시제 · 내용

items.text: Hold the seasonal grave rite each year for ancestors of the fourth generation and above, at the appointed times.
items.citation: Encyclopedia of Korean Folk Culture, 시제 時祭 · 시제 · 내용
items.quote: 묘제의는 3월 상순에 날을 가려 일년에 한 번 제사를 지내며 — On the first ten days of the third month they choose a day and perform the rite once a year.
items.conflict: Conflicts with the First Commandment: worship belongs to God alone (Ex 20:3-5); honoring ancestors should not include sacrificial offerings or ritual bows to the dead.

items.text: As master of the rite, prepare in advance, fast, bring stewards, clean the grave, and offer the first cup and incense.
items.citation: Encyclopedia of Korean Folk Culture, 시제 時祭 · 시제 · 내용
items.quote: 하루 전날 주인이 여러 집사자들을 거느리고 묘사로 나아가 재계한다... 묘소와 그 주변을 청소한다 — The day before, the master goes with stewards to the grave-house and fasts... he cleans the grave and surroundings.
items.conflict: Conflicts with the First Commandment: worship belongs to God alone (Ex 20:3-5); honoring ancestors should not include sacrificial offerings or ritual bows to the dead.

items.text: All who attend the grave rite bow twice to the ancestors at the beginning and at the end.
items.citation: Encyclopedia of Korean Folk Culture, 시제 時祭 · 시제 · 내용
items.quote: 참사자 모두 참신 재배를 한다... 참사자 모두 사신 재배를 한다 — All participants do the two bows of greeting... all do the two bows of farewell.
items.conflict: Conflicts with the First Commandment: worship belongs to God alone (Ex 20:3-5); honoring ancestors should not include sacrificial offerings or ritual bows to the dead.

items.text: Offer the second cup (or third) at the ancestral grave rite.
items.citation: Encyclopedia of Korean Folk Culture, 시제 時祭 · 시제 · 내용
items.quote: 아헌과 종헌은 모두 아들 또는 동생이나 친한 벗이 한다 — The second and third offerings are made by a son, a younger brother, or a close friend.
items.conflict: Conflicts with the First Commandment: worship belongs to God alone (Ex 20:3-5); honoring ancestors should not include sacrificial offerings or ritual bows to the dead.

items.text: Offer the second cup (or third) at the ancestral grave rite, as a younger brother.
items.citation: Encyclopedia of Korean Folk Culture, 시제 時祭 · 시제 · 내용
items.quote: 아헌과 종헌은 모두 아들 또는 동생이나 친한 벗이 한다 — The second and third offerings are made by a son, a younger brother, or a close friend.
items.conflict: Conflicts with the First Commandment: worship belongs to God alone (Ex 20:3-5); honoring ancestors should not include sacrificial offerings or ritual bows to the dead.

work: Encyclopedia of Korean Folk Culture: articles on lineage, succession, adoption,
heading: 양자 養子 … 참고문헌

items.text: Care for your adoptive parents in their old age.
items.citation: Encyclopedia of Korean Folk Culture, 양자 養子
items.quote: 노후 봉양과 사후 제사를 맡기기도 — entrusting support in old age and posthumous rites

items.text: Offer the posthumous rites for your adoptive parents.
items.citation: Encyclopedia of Korean Folk Culture, 양자 養子
items.quote: 사후 제사를 맡기기도 — entrusting posthumous rites
items.conflict: Ancestor worship; first commandment

items.text: Mourn your adoptive parents and adoptive kin with the full mourning of biological parents and kin.
items.citation: Encyclopedia of Korean Folk Culture, 양자 養子
items.quote: 양부모와 양가養家 친족에게 친부모 및 친가 친족에 해당하는 상복을 입고 — wear for adoptive parents and adoptive kin the mourning of biological parents and kin
items.conflict: Confucian mourning rites may include ancestor veneration; Deut 18:9-12

items.text: Mourn your biological parents and kin with mourning one grade lower.
items.citation: Encyclopedia of Korean Folk Culture, 양자 養子
items.quote: 친가 부모와 친족에게는 한 등급을 강복降服하도록 하였다 — for biological parents and kin, reduce mourning by one grade
items.conflict: Confucian mourning rites may include ancestor veneration; Deut 18:9-12
